title: First ALMA maps of HCO, an important precursor of complex organic molecules, towards IRAS 16293-2422
question: Where and how is the formyl radical HCO formed in IRAS 16293-2422 (envelope gas-phase vs hot corino grain surface), and what is its role as precursor of H2CO, CH3OH and glycolaldehyde?

data.angular_resolution: synthesized beams ~1.25-1.45 x 0.90-1.04 arcsec per spw; continuum 1.09x0.78 arcsec

what.value: Dust absorption coefficient 0.009 cm2/g at 1 mm (thin ices, n=1e6 cm-3)

evidence.quote: extrapolating from the value at 1 mm of 0.009 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ (thin ices in a H$_2$ density of 10$^6$ cm$^{-3}$; see (cite: ossenkopf94))

what.value: Cold envelope N(H2)=2e23 cm-2 and 10 K temperature

evidence.quote: we used molecular entries from JPL[^4] ((cite: pickett1998)) and CDMS[^5]

what.value: Desorption energies HCO 1600 K and CH2OHCHO 6684 K

evidence.quote: has much higher desorption energy than HCO (6684 K vs. 1600 K; (cite: garrod08))

recipe.goal: Fit continuum level and derive N(H2)
recipe.method: Modified blackbody fit by visual inspection varying beta and tau_d0 over four spws; T_c fixed to CH3OH Tex; N(H2) from tau_d0
assumptions: gas-to-dust 100; mu=2.8; kappa0 extrapolated from 0.009 cm2/g at 1 mm

recipe.goal: Measure source sizes and identify lines
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fits for sizes; SLIM line identification with JPL/CDMS; Gaussian line fits
key_parameters: Molecular emission size assumed equal to continuum: 0.88 arcsec (A), 0.44 arcsec (B)
assumptions: Line emission unresolved, same size as continuum

recipe.goal: Derive column densities, Tex and abundances via LTE
recipe.method: MADCUBA-AUTOFIT LTE fits of emission and absorption components with Levenberg-Marquardt; abundances relative to N(H2)
key_parameters: Free: N, Tex, v, FWHM; HCO Tex assumed 50-180 K; absorption 10 K; H2CO Tex 100 K

recipe.method: Integrate ALMA over 28 arcsec IRAM beam and compare; fit extended HCO with LTE at 10 K
assumptions: Emission fills the telescope beam; Tex 10 K

recipe.method: 0-D gas-grain model with collapse and warm-up; models I-III for HCO formation; CH2OHCHO via HCO+CH2OH; abundance uncertainty factor of 3
key_parameters: Collapse 1e6 yr, n 3e3 to 1e8 cm-3; warm-up 10-200 K over 2e5 yr

evidence.quote: We obtained N(H2)=4.4$\times$10$^{24}$ cm$^{-2}$ and N(H2)=5.0$\times$10$^{25}$ cm$^{-2}$ for A and B, respectively.
We obtained N(H2)=4.4$\times$10$^{24}$ cm$^{-2}$ and N(H2)=5.0$\times$10$^{25}$ cm$^{-2}$ for A and B, respectively.
For source A, the HCO abundance is (0.06$-$0.36)$\times$10$^{-8}$, for the range of excitation temperature considered.
For source B, the HCO abundance is (0.01$-$0.06)$\times$10$^{-8}$
We obtained a temperature of 157$\pm$14 K for source B
which translates into an abundance of (1.5$-$2.9)$\times$10$^{-11}$
